aiReview.summary: Official Google AI for Developers hub covering Gemini API docs, pricing, AI Studio, Gemma, and related tools. Direct primary documentation for Gemini developers.
evidence: canonicalUrl https://ai.google.dev is Google’s official developer portal.
Excerpt lists Gemini docs, API reference, pricing, AI Studio, Gemma, and responsible AI.
riskFlags empty; source official-web with high confidenceScore.
uncertainty: Exact current free-tier vs paid API limits not fully specified in the excerpt.
Page excerpt is truncated so some homepage sections are incomplete.
aiReview.tagline: Official docs, API, and Studio for Google AI models
aiReview.description: Browse Gemini, Imagen, Veo, and Gemma docs, API reference, pricing, AI Studio, and on-device options from Google.
pros: Canonical official site with Gemini API docs, API reference, and pricing links.
Points to Google AI Studio for model exploration and prompting.
Includes Gemma open-model docs plus Imagen, Veo, Edge, and responsible-AI resources.
cons: Homepage is a navigation hub rather than a single implementation tutorial.
API usage itself is billed per Google’s pricing, not fully free.

aiReview.summary: Open-source Kotlin sample that wires Google Generative AI / Gemini into a Jetpack Compose Android chat app using Stream Chat. Useful as an architecture demo; requires Stream and Gemini keys and is not a standalone SDK.
evidence: GitHub description: demonstrates Google Generative AI on Android with Stream Chat SDK for Compose; 386 stars, Apache-2.0, Kotlin.
README purpose list includes Gemini API for Android and Stream Chat Compose for real-time events.
Build steps require STREAM_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY in secrets.properties.
CI badge points at .github/workflows/android.yml.
uncertainty: Recency of last commit and whether generative-ai Android SDK versions are current.
Whether listed issues (12) include security or key-handling problems.
Production readiness of disabling Stream authentication as instructed.
aiReview.tagline: Compose Android sample for Gemini chat with Stream
aiReview.description: Shows Gemini API usage on Android with Jetpack Compose, Hilt, and Stream Chat. Follow the README to add keys and run the sample.
pros: README documents Gemini API key setup via Google AI Studio and links the Android Gemini quickstart.
Includes CI workflows, Apache-2.0 license, modular Gradle structure, and Google-style UI/data architecture.
Demonstrates Compose UI, Hilt, coroutines, and real-time chat integration rather than a single snippet.
cons: Build depends on Stream Chat API keys and disabling Stream auth checks, not Gemini alone.
Canonical listing URL skydoves/gemini-android redirects to GetStream/gemini-android.
Sample app, not a reusable client library.

uncertainty: Whether the published npm package still works against current Gemini endpoints and model names.
Issue/PR activity quality beyond four open issues listed on the GitHub overview.
aiReview.tagline: Thin JS wrapper for simpler Gemini REST calls

Third-party REST wrapper is not Google-maintained and may diverge from @google/generative-ai.

aiReview.summary: Community MIT Ruby gem that wraps Gemini via Vertex AI, Generative Language API, and AI Studio with streaming, embeddings, tools, and safety docs. Last push was mid-2025, so confirm it still matches current Gemini models before production use.
evidence: GitHub description and README: Ruby gem for Vertex AI, Generative Language API, or AI Studio.
facts: MIT license, 190 stars, not archived, pushed_at 2025-07-09.
README covers streaming SSE, embeddings, system instructions, JSON, and function calling.
uncertainty: Whether gem 4.3.0 tracks latest Gemini 2.x models and REST changes.
Issue quality and security review of credential handling were not audited in depth.
aiReview.tagline: Ruby client for Vertex, Generative Language, and AI Studio
aiReview.description: Call Gemini from Ruby with API keys or Vertex credentials, including streaming, embeddings, JSON, and function calling.
pros: README documents Generative Language API keys, Vertex service accounts, ADC, and a global endpoint.
Supports stream_generate_content, generate_content, embeddings, token counting, JSON schema, tools, and safety settings.
MIT-licensed Ruby gem with specs and a published version (~> 4.3.0).
cons: Repository last push was 2025-07-09, so model names and APIs may lag official Gemini.
Unofficial community client; 19 open issues and default examples still use gemini-pro.
Credential setup docs include IAM policy-binding commands that can expand Google Cloud access if misused.

evidence: README states Gemini Pro vs Pro Vision routing, /start new chat, and contextual understanding for Pro.
Facts: MIT, not archived, topics include gemini-pro and telegram-bot; pushed_at 2024-10-18; ~29–31 stars.
File list is a single script.py plus Docker/shell helpers, not a library or maintained product.
uncertainty: Actual API client version, key handling in config.json, and whether gemini-pro still works were not verified in code.
Current runtime health of the Docker image and Telegram bot behavior was not tested.
aiReview.tagline: Self-hosted Telegram bot wrapping Gemini Pro and Vision
aiReview.description: Run a personal Telegram bot that routes text to Gemini Pro and images to Gemini Pro Vision, with Docker or Ubuntu install scripts.
pros: Uses Google Gemini Pro for text and Gemini Pro Vision for image-plus-text without a manual model switch.
Documents obtaining a Gemini API key from Google AI Studio (makersuite) and a Telegram BotFather token.
Ships MIT license, Dockerfile, setup scripts, and short bilingual README with sample screenshots.
cons: Repository activity stopped around 2024-10-18 with low stars and no issues, so models and APIs may be outdated.
Install flow relies on wget of remote shell scripts and a config.json volume with little security or production guidance.

aiReview.summary: Deprecated community frontend chat UI for the Gemini API; useful as a historical demo, not as a maintained developer resource.
evidence: GitHub README titled Deprecated: intended for early Gemini when no UI existed; no longer maintained.
Repo metadata: TypeScript, MIT, ~69 stars, ~24 forks; files include Chat page, Docker, Caddyfile.
README: API key and name stored in browser; requests go to Google; live demo on Vercel.
Canonical URL github.com/fjosue4/google-gemini-ui now maps to fjosue4/deprecated-google-gemini-ui.
uncertainty: Last commit date and whether the Vercel demo still works were not verified beyond the README.
Whether the Gemini API usage matches current SDK/auth patterns was not code-reviewed in depth.
aiReview.tagline: Browser chat UI that talks directly to Gemini
aiReview.description: Pure front-end chat client that stores an API key in the browser and calls Google servers, with Docker and Vercel deploy notes.
pros: MIT-licensed TypeScript/Vite chat app that calls the Gemini API from the browser.
README documents local npm, Docker Compose, and Vercel deploy paths.
Includes changelog items for API-key feedback, chat history, light mode, and optional request proxy.
cons: The README states the project is deprecated and will no longer be maintained.
It was built for early Gemini and is not positioned as current official tooling.
Client-side API key storage and optional proxy increase operational and security caveats.

aiReview.summary: Dec 2023 Google Cloud Community tutorial on Cloud Code/VS Code templates that scaffold Node or Python apps calling the Gemini API with a Google AI Studio key. Useful as a beginner walkthrough, but it is a short Medium post using outdated model names (gemini-pro) and Cloud Shell steps that may not match current tooling.
evidence: canonicalUrl is a Medium Google Cloud post titled Getting Started with Gemini AI API via Google Cloud Code Application Templates.
Body requires GCP project/billing, Cloud Code New Application, Gemini API Python/Node templates, and AI Studio API key.
Sample run lists models/gemini-pro and models/gemini-pro-vision.
uncertainty: Whether Cloud Code still ships the same Gemini templates.
Whether Medium full text remains freely readable for all users.
aiReview.tagline: Cloud Code templates to try the Gemini API in VS Code
aiReview.description: Walk through Cloud Code app templates in Cloud Shell or VS Code to run a Python or Node sample against the Gemini API.
pros: Published on Google Cloud Community by Romin Irani with concrete Cloud Code and AI Studio steps.
Shows New Application templates for Node.js and Python and how to set GOOGLE_API_KEY.
Includes install, run, and a sample generate-content prompt using google-generativeai.
cons: Article is from December 2023 and references gemini-pro / MakerSuite-era AI Studio.
Paywalled or truncated Medium reading can block full access without an account.
Does not cover current Gemini model IDs, Vertex AI, or production hardening.

aiReview.summary: Dec 2023 Medium walkthrough of an Apps Script custom function that calls Vertex AI gemini-pro from Google Sheets; useful as a dated integration example, not as current Gemini API guidance.
evidence: Published 2023-12-19; title and body use Gemini Pro / Vertex AI streamGenerateContent.
Endpoint pattern: .../publishers/google/models/gemini-pro:streamGenerateContent.
auth() stores ScriptApp.getOAuthToken() in CacheService; askGemini reads it for Bearer auth.
Article is ~4 minutes; assumes basic Apps Script knowledge.
uncertainty: Whether Medium paywall or edits changed the full code for some readers.
Whether the sample still works against current Vertex Gemini APIs.
Exact error handling beyond returning ERROR on non-200.
aiReview.tagline: Apps Script custom function calling Vertex AI Gemini
aiReview.description: Shows OAuth, UrlFetchApp, and a Sheets custom function that posts prompts to Vertex AI gemini-pro and returns the first response chunk.
pros: Describes a complete path from GCP project and Vertex AI enablement to an Apps Script askGemini custom function.
Includes oauthScopes, token caching via CacheService, and a UrlFetchApp POST to the Vertex generateContent-style endpoint.
Notes Sheets recalculation can re-hit the API and suggests guarding with IF().
Links Vertex model reference and a GCP quickstart for project setup.
cons: Targets Vertex AI gemini-pro from December 2023, not the current Gemini Developer API or model names.
Code uses undeclared PROJECT_ID/REGION placeholders and parses only json[0] of streamGenerateContent.
Logs the OAuth token and stores it in user cache; custom functions cannot complete interactive auth themselves.
Pricing and free-tier claims are snapshot-dated and may be wrong today.

aiReview.summary: A 2023 Medium walkthrough that wires @google/generative-ai into a Vite React bedtime-story form. Useful as a beginner demo, but it hardcodes the API key in the browser, uses the deprecated gemini-pro model and Maker Suite naming, and the sample code has typos.
evidence: Article published 2023-12-15 on Medium by Udara Liyanage; 4 min read.
Code uses GoogleGenerativeAI from @google/generative-ai and model gemini-pro.
Prerequisites link to makersuite.google.com/app/apikey.
Demo URL: https://bedtime-story-udarax.netlify.app/
API key placeholder is passed directly to the client constructor.
uncertainty: Whether the Netlify demo still works and whether it ships a live key.
Full remaining article content after the truncated App.jsx section.
Author updates or GitHub companion repo quality.
aiReview.tagline: Beginner Vite React demo calling Gemini for stories
aiReview.description: Build a Vite React bedtime-story form that calls Gemini via @google/generative-ai, with a Netlify demo and copy-paste App.jsx.
pros: Shows installing @google/generative-ai and calling getGenerativeModel plus generateContent from a Vite React app.
Includes a public Netlify demo of the bedtime-story form.
Covers obtaining an API key and a short project setup sequence with npm create vite.
cons: Embeds YOUR-API-KEY-HERE in client-side App.jsx, which would expose a real key in the browser.
Targets the old gemini-pro model and Google Maker Suite rather than current Gemini API docs.
Sample HTML/JSX includes typos (e.g. extra characters after </html>) and marketing-heavy, shallow steps.
Published December 2023 with no maintenance signals in the article itself.

aiReview.summary: A short Google Cloud Community Medium tutorial showing SwiftUI multi-turn chat via the Gemini iOS SDK Chat object and gemini-pro. Useful for learning, but dated (gemini-pro, vision chat caveats) and not a maintained product.
evidence: Canonical URL is a Google Cloud Community Medium article by Anup D'Souza on multi-turn Gemini chat in SwiftUI.
Article quotes Gemini docs on Chat managing conversation state versus generateContent.
Code snippets initialize GenerativeModel(name: "gemini-pro") and chat.sendMessage; complete code linked to github.com/anupdsouza/ios-gemini-chat.
og:description matches SDK multi-turn chat value proposition.
uncertainty: Whether the GitHub sample still compiles against current GoogleGenerativeAI / Firebase AI SDK versions.
How API keys are stored in the sample (not fully visible in the article).
Medium full-text access may differ for signed-out readers.
aiReview.tagline: SwiftUI tutorial for multi-turn Gemini chat on iOS
aiReview.description: Walks through Gemini Chat, history, and sendMessage in SwiftUI, with sample code for a text-only iOS chat UI.
pros: Published in Google Cloud Community and covers the official Gemini iOS SDK Chat/startChat/sendMessage flow.
Explains conversation history via ModelContent roles and points to a GitHub sample (ios-gemini-chat).
Notes the then-current limitation that gemini-pro-vision was not suited for multi-turn chat.
cons: Uses the older gemini-pro model name and is a ~3-minute 2023 post that may not match current Gemini APIs.
Medium paywall/signup friction and promotional YouTube/social links reduce it as a durable docs source.
Does not cover production concerns such as API key handling beyond APIKey.default.

uncertainty: Whether the Medium author has permission beyond the stated original publication note.
Current availability of Bard/Gemini consumer features described in the article.
aiReview.tagline: 2023 news recap of Google’s Gemini model launch
aiReview.description: Summarizes Gemini Nano, Pro, and Ultra, Bard, and GPT-4 comparisons from a 2023 launch article, without API or coding guidance.
pros: Covers Gemini Nano, Pro, and Ultra product positioning at launch.

cons: No Gemini API, SDK, or implementation content for developers.

aiReview.summary: Short Google Cloud Community tutorial (Dec 2023) showing Vertex AI Java SDK usage for multimodal generateContent, streaming, and ChatSession. Useful as a Java starter, but model IDs and BOM versions are dated.
evidence: Article dated Dec 13/18 2023 on medium.com/google-cloud.
Code uses VertexAI, GenerativeModel("gemini-pro-vision"), ContentMaker/PartMaker, generateContentStream, ChatSession.
Canonical also at glaforge.dev; author helped with Java samples/SDK.
uncertainty: Whether snippets still compile against current Vertex AI Java SDK.
Paywall or Medium login friction for some readers.
aiReview.tagline: Java Vertex AI samples for multimodal LLM calls
aiReview.description: Walks through Maven setup, multimodal generateContent, streaming, and ChatSession with google-cloud-vertexai.
pros: Published in Google Cloud Community by a Google Cloud Developer Advocate.
Includes concrete Maven BOM/google-cloud-vertexai setup and Java snippets.
Covers multimodal image+text prompts, streaming, and ChatSession.
Links to official Vertex AI docs and java-docs-samples on GitHub.
cons: Uses outdated model names such as gemini-pro-vision.
Pins an old libraries-bom (26.29.0) and is a 3-minute 2023 snapshot.
Targets Vertex AI on GCP, not the consumer Gemini Developer API.

aiReview.summary: ArXiv survey (Dec 2023) on generative AI landscape, MoE, multimodality, and AGI speculation; it mentions Google’s Gemini as context, not as a Gemini API or implementation guide.
evidence: arXiv:2312.10868 abstract focuses on MoE, multimodal learning, AGI, and research taxonomy rather than API docs.
Candidate type is web_url to abs/2312.10868 discovered from an awesome-list README, not official Google AI docs.
No code, SDK, or CLI is associated with this candidate.
uncertainty: Peer-review status and citation quality were not independently verified beyond the arXiv abstract.
Full PDF was not scored line-by-line for factual accuracy of Gemini claims.
aiReview.tagline: Academic survey of generative AI research directions
aiReview.description: Reviews generative AI trends including MoE, multimodality, AGI speculation, ethics, and preprint/peer-review issues; not an API how-to.
pros: Hosted on arXiv with an abstract covering generative AI, MoE, multimodality, and ethics.
Explicitly discusses Google’s Gemini in a research-landscape context rather than marketing copy.
Addresses scholarly-communication issues around AI-themed and AI-generated preprints.
cons: Does not document Gemini API usage, SDKs, or implementation patterns.
Dated December 2023, so it predates later Gemini API and model releases.
Broad AGI/Q* speculation is a poor fit for a developer-resource directory.

aiReview.summary: Paid Udemy course on using ChatGPT and Gemini chat tools for social media marketing, not Gemini API or developer implementation. Weak fit for a Gemini developer resource list.
evidence: canonicalUrl is a Udemy course page, not GitHub or Google AI docs.
What you'll learn lists social content, Canva, Meta ads, InVideo—not Gemini API.
Course title/meta mention Google Gemini AI alongside ChatGPT for social media.
uncertainty: Full lecture accuracy and whether any Gemini API code is taught.
Current price and instructor maintenance beyond last-updated date.
Whether content is mostly ChatGPT with Gemini as a thin add-on.
aiReview.tagline: Learn consumer AI prompts for multi-platform social content
aiReview.description: Teaches ChatGPT and Gemini prompting for Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, and related social workflows. Paid Udemy course, not an API or SDK.
pros: Udemy listing is live with 16h of lectures, 144 items, last updated 9/2025.
Curriculum covers prompting Gemini/ChatGPT for social posts, calendars, and several platforms.
Public ratings exist (about 4.2 from 39 ratings) and thousands of enrollments.
cons: Focus is consumer chat and marketing, not Gemini API, SDKs, or production code.
Title still markets a dated “2024/2026” growth course rather than developer docs.
Lesson quality and API accuracy cannot be verified without buying the course.

aiReview.summary: Paid Udemy course on generative AI for software/QA engineers; Gemini is one of several tools (ChatGPT, Bard) and is not a focused Gemini API implementation resource.
evidence: canonicalUrl is a Udemy course; meta title is Accelerated Software Engineering Chat GPT and AI Agents.
Learning outcomes list Main Features of Google GEMINI AI alongside OPENAI CHATGPT, Google BARD, JMeter, REST Assured.
10,602 students, 4.4/5, last updated 9/2025.
uncertainty: Cannot verify lecture accuracy, Gemini API version used, or whether Bard content was fully migrated.
Exact price and refund terms not captured from the page scrape.
aiReview.tagline: Paid course on gen-AI for software and QA engineers
aiReview.description: Teaches ChatGPT, Gemini/Bard, and agents for testing, CI/CD, and engineering workflows via practical examples.
pros: Udemy listing shows 11h 24m across 159 lectures with a 4.4 rating from 3,218 ratings.
Curriculum includes Gemini/Bard features plus ChatGPT API, CI/CD, and QA/test-framework examples.
Last updated September 2025 according to the course page.
cons: Slug and many outcomes still center ChatGPT and Google Bard, so Gemini API coverage looks secondary and dated.
Paid marketplace course, not official docs or open implementation samples.
Title mismatch between list anchor, URL, and on-page name reduces catalog reliability.

aiReview.summary: Paid Udemy beginner course on consumer chat UIs (ChatGPT, Gemini/Bard, Bing/Copilot) and prompting, not Gemini API or developer tooling. Weak fit for a Gemini developer directory.
evidence: canonicalUrl is a Udemy course titled Master 3 AI Chatbots in 1 Course: ChatGPT, Gemini, Bing Chat.
Meta description: Learn the full potential of ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot with powerful prompts.
What you'll learn bullets emphasize Bing Chat, Edge, Bard travel/fitness/email, and ChatGPT conversations—not APIs.
7 sections, 53 lectures, 2h 13m; rating 3.9/5; last updated 8/2025.
uncertainty: Full lecture quality and accuracy of Gemini vs Bard content not independently verified.
Exact current price after Udemy discounts unknown.
How much of the runtime is actually Gemini versus ChatGPT/Bing is unclear from the outline.
aiReview.tagline: Beginner prompts for ChatGPT, Gemini, and Bing Chat
aiReview.description: Teaches consumer chatbot use, prompting, and Bing Image Creator across ChatGPT, Gemini/Bard, and Copilot in a short paid course.
pros: Course page lists Gemini/Bard alongside ChatGPT and Bing Chat with last update in August 2025.
Curriculum covers chatbot setup, prompting, and consumer productivity use cases.
Public ratings (3.9/5 from 203 reviews) and ~15k enrollments are visible on Udemy.
cons: Does not teach Gemini API, SDKs, or developer implementation.
Learning objectives skew heavily to Bing Chat, Edge, and generic ChatGPT, with Bard/Gemini as consumer chat.
URL and content still reference Google Bard; lectures include unofficial “GPT-4 for free” workarounds.
Paid marketplace course, not official Google documentation.

Candidate was discovered only as a README Amazon link, not as a GitHub/docs resource.
uncertainty: Full book contents, accuracy vs current Gemini API, and reader ratings were not fully inspectable.
Whether any practical integration steps exist beyond marketing claims.

Suitable as background reading on model behavior, not as an integration resource.
cons: Does not document the Gemini API, SDKs, or implementation patterns.

aiReview.summary: Third-party 2023 arXiv paper comparing Gemini Pro vs GPT-3.5 Turbo on 10 language tasks, with linked reproduction code. Useful historical evaluation, not a current Gemini API implementation guide.
evidence: arXiv:2312.11444 abstract describes third-party Gemini vs GPT comparison and github.com/neulab/gemini-benchmark.
Submission history shows v1 2023-12-18 and v2 2023-12-24 only.
Listed in an Awesome Google Gemini curated README as a language-abilities paper.
uncertainty: Whether the GitHub benchmark repo is still maintained or runnable against current APIs.
Citation impact and whether later errata exist beyond v2.
aiReview.tagline: Third-party 2023 language-task comparison vs GPT-3.5
aiReview.description: Compares Gemini Pro and GPT-3.5 Turbo on 10 language tasks with public code; notes strengths, failures, and filtering behavior.
pros: Peer-style arXiv paper with a clear abstract and stated methodology over 10 datasets.
Includes a public GitHub repo (neulab/gemini-benchmark) for reproduction.
Documents observed failure modes such as digit-heavy math, MCQ order sensitivity, and content filtering.
cons: Last revised December 2023, so results do not cover later Gemini models or the current developer API.
It is an evaluation paper, not SDK, CLI, or integration documentation.
Findings are limited to Gemini Pro vs GPT-3.5 Turbo on the authors’ chosen tasks.

aiReview.summary: Peer-reviewed-style arXiv paper (Dec 2023) comparing Gemini Pro vision to GPT-4V and Sphinx; useful background, not an API or implementation guide.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.12436 abstract: preliminary exploration of Gemini Pro visual understanding vs GPT-4V and Sphinx; MME benchmark; project https://github.com/BradyFU/Awesome-Multimodal-Large-Language-Models
Submitted 19 Dec 2023, v2 20 Dec 2023; ~120 pages; nonexclusive arXiv license
uncertainty: Peer-review/venue status beyond arXiv not verified
Whether code or prompts from the paper are maintained
aiReview.tagline: Early qualitative/quantitative Gemini Pro vision study
aiReview.description: Compares Gemini Pro visual understanding with GPT-4V and Sphinx across perception, cognition, and expert tasks, plus MME scores.
pros: arXiv cs.CV paper with abstract, PDF, and HTML covering Gemini Pro visual evaluation versus GPT-4V and Sphinx.
Describes four evaluation domains plus MME quantitative comparison and observed MLLM failure modes.
Links a related GitHub list for tracking multimodal LLM progress.
cons: Not a Gemini API, SDK, or developer tutorial; last revised 20 Dec 2023 so findings may be outdated.
Uses Gemini Pro as a black-box product, not implementation patterns for builders.

aiReview.summary: Peer-reviewed arXiv evaluation of Gemini (and other LLMs/MLLMs) on commonsense reasoning benchmarks, not an API, SDK, or implementation guide. Useful background on model behavior; limited value as a hands-on Gemini developer resource.
evidence: Abstract: thorough evaluation on 12 commonsense datasets (11 language-only, 1 multimodal) and experiments on four LLMs and two MLLMs.
Canonical URL is arxiv.org/abs/2312.17661; authors Yuqing Wang, Yun Zhao; published 2023-12-29.
Candidate is a research paper, not a tool or client library.
uncertainty: Peer-review/venue status beyond arXiv listing not verified.
Code or data release for the experiments not confirmed from the abstract page.
How the source awesome-list section categorizes this link beyond the paper title.
aiReview.tagline: Benchmark study of multimodal commonsense reasoning
aiReview.description: Evaluates multimodal and language models on 12 commonsense reasoning datasets and reports competitive results plus remaining failure modes.
pros: arXiv cs.CL/cs.AI/cs.CV paper (2312.17661) with a clear abstract and stated experimental scope.
Compares four LLMs and two MLLMs across 12 commonsense datasets, including one multimodal set.
Discusses gaps versus GPT-class models and shared failure modes rather than only headline scores.
cons: No Gemini API, SDK, or sample code for implementers.
Dated December 2023, so findings may not match current Gemini model versions.
HellaSWAG-limited prior claims are addressed academically, not as a maintained developer tutorial.

evidence: Canonical URL is pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38355668.
Title and abstract describe Gemini vs ChatGPT comparative analysis in ophthalmology.
MeSH terms include Ophthalmology, Artificial Intelligence, Search Engine; no developer-resource signals.
uncertainty: Full-text methods, which Gemini product/version was tested, and paywall vs PMC full text were not fully verified.
Fit depends on whether the target list includes research papers versus only buildable Gemini resources.

aiReview.description: Compares Gemini and ChatGPT on ophthalmology tasks in a 2024 Eye paper; useful as background reading, not as API or coding guidance.

Authors declare no competing interests on the PubMed record.

PubMed listing provides citation metadata rather than implementation tutorials.

aiReview.summary: Official Google YouTube demo (Dec 2023) showing multimodal reasoning across text, images, audio, video, and code. Useful as background context, not as an API, SDK, or implementation guide; the description notes shortened outputs and reduced latency.
evidence: YouTube title: The capabilities of multimodal AI | Gemini Demo; channel Google; uploaded 2023-12-06.
Description states natively multimodal reasoning across text, images, audio, video and code and points to https://deepmind.google/gemini.
Candidate type is web_url discovered from a curated awesome README, not a code repository.
uncertainty: Whether the linked DeepMind try page still matches the demoed behavior.
How well this belongs in a developer-focused Gemini API directory versus a general media list.
aiReview.tagline: Official 6-minute multimodal capability showcase
aiReview.description: Watch Google’s 2023 multimodal demo covering dialogue, vision, games, spatial reasoning, and generation, with a DeepMind try link.
pros: Published on the Google YouTube channel with 3.3M views and a 6:22 runtime.
Description links to deepmind.google/gemini and a related how-it’s-made video.
Chapters cover multimodal dialogue, multilinguality, visual puzzles, logic, and cultural understanding.
cons: It is a marketing demo, not developer documentation, code, or Gemini API usage.
The video discloses that latency was reduced and outputs were shortened for the demo.
Content dates to December 2023 and may not match current model APIs or product surfaces.

Description promotes trying Bard and learning about Bard with Gemini Pro.
Transcript is a science-entertainment collab (paper airplane through a ring of fire), not an implementation walkthrough.
uncertainty: Whether Bard URLs still redirect to Gemini.
Whether the awesome-list intends consumer videos versus developer resources.
aiReview.tagline: Consumer demo of Bard collaborating on a science video
aiReview.description: Watch a 2023 Google clip where Bard with Gemini Pro helps design and test a paper airplane, not an API tutorial.
pros: Official Google channel upload from 2023-12-06 with about 30 million views.
Shows multimodal/chat collaboration with Bard (Gemini Pro) in a real creative workflow.
Description and transcript are public and match the listed title.
cons: No Gemini API, SDK, code, or developer documentation.
Product branding is Bard; the experience is outdated relative to current Gemini APIs.
Links in the description point at bard.google.com rather than AI Studio or the developer docs.

aiReview.summary: Unofficial 2023 walkthrough of integrating Gemini into an Android sample that sends a room photo plus text for furniture suggestions. Useful as a short intro, but API setup, models, and billing details are dated and not a maintained SDK or official sample.
evidence: YouTube i7PJwg0lrU0, Philipp Lackner, 8:13, ~131K views, 2023-12-27.
Description and captions describe Android Gemini furniture-suggestion app and generateContent with bitmap plus prompt.
Listed repeatedly in Curated-Awesome-Lists/Awesome-Google-Gemini-AI README with no extra docs.
uncertainty: Whether companion GitHub code still exists or matches current Gemini Android SDK.
Accuracy of stated free-tier and 60 RPS billing compared with current Google AI pricing.
aiReview.tagline: Short Android walkthrough of Gemini vision prompts
aiReview.description: Watch an Android sample send an image and text to Gemini for furniture suggestions, covering API key setup and generateContent.
pros: Shows Android Studio Gemini starter wizard, GenerativeModel, and generateContent with image plus text.
Demonstrates a concrete vision use case: room photo to furniture suggestions.
Transcript covers Pro vs Nano vs Ultra at announcement time and reading response text/candidates.
cons: Uploaded 2023-12-27; model names, MakerSuite, Iguana preview, and billing claims are outdated.
No linked source repo or maintained sample in the listing facts.
Mentions VPN for regional access and putting payment info on the API, which can mislead beginners.

aiReview.summary: Official Google DeepMind demo (Dec 2023) of Gemini filtering ~200k papers and extracting data; promotional product video, not a developer API or implementation guide.
evidence: YouTube metadata: Google channel, uploaded 2023-12-06, duration 2:42, video sPiOP_CB54A.
Description and transcript describe filtering 200,000 papers to ~250 and extracting tables/annotations.
No code, API keys, or SDK walkthrough in the page content.
uncertainty: Whether the linked blog/demos still match current Gemini API behavior.
Exact model version used in the demo is not specified.
aiReview.tagline: Official demo of large-scale scientific paper filtering
aiReview.description: Watch DeepMind staff use Gemini to filter 200k papers, extract data, and update a figure in a short product demo.
pros: Published on the official Google YouTube channel with a transcript.
Shows a concrete literature-filtering and extraction workflow plus a figure-update example.
Links out to Gemini demos, DeepMind Gemini pages, and a blog post.
cons: Does not document Gemini API, SDKs, or runnable sample code.
Two-minute 2023 promo; capabilities and APIs may be outdated.
Weak fit for a developer-resource directory versus a general Gemini showcase.

aiReview.summary: Third-party Feb 2024 news recap of Gemini 1.5 (context window, Vertex/AI Studio preview, Firebase extensions). It is not a maintained developer guide or official API resource, so it is a weak fit for an awesome Gemini developer list.
evidence: Page title and body: Google unveils Gemini 1.5 with million-token context; published Feb 16, 2024 by Mauricio B. Holguin on AlternativeTo.
Article cites Vertex AI preview, AI Studio waitlist form, and Firebase extensions Build Chatbot / Multimodal Tasks with Gemini API.
External links include blog.google Gemini 1.5 announcement and firebase.blog Gemini post.
Candidate type is web_url discovered from a curated README, not a code repository.
uncertainty: Whether the AI Studio waitlist URL and Firebase extension IDs still work.
Accuracy of secondary claims versus the official Google blog at time of publication.
aiReview.tagline: Feb 2024 recap of Gemini 1.5 launch claims
aiReview.description: Summarizes Gemini 1.5 efficiency, million-token context, Vertex/AI Studio preview, and Firebase Gemini extensions with links to official posts.
pros: Reports Gemini 1.5 claims: efficiency vs Gemini 1.0 Ultra and an experimental million-token context window.
Mentions Vertex AI limited preview, an AI Studio waitlist, and two Firebase Gemini API extensions with outbound links.
Lists official sources including Google’s Gemini 1.5 blog, a Firebase blog post, and a YouTube demo.
cons: It is a short AlternativeTo news article from 16 Feb 2024, not SDK, API docs, or a tutorial.
Launch-era details (waitlist, preview availability) are stale relative to current Gemini APIs.
Content is secondary journalism with ads/partner placements rather than first-party implementation guidance.

No SDK, CLI, or API reference is present in the candidate facts.
uncertainty: Episode audio and shownotes were not retrieved (Apple page redirected).
Accuracy and depth of technical claims in the episode are unverified.
aiReview.tagline: Daily AI news episode on Gemini 1.5 context length

pros: Episode slug explicitly references Gemini 1.5 and a one-million-token context window.
Hosted on Apple Podcasts as a dated news episode rather than an unofficial API wrapper.
cons: It is a third-party news podcast, not official Gemini API documentation or sample code.
The listing is a single episode URL, not a maintained developer tutorial or SDK.
Apple Podcasts geo/redirect behavior can hide the original episode page.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud hub that compares Gemini Developer API, Gemini platform, Enterprise editions, and in-product assistants. Useful as an entry map, but it is a marketing/comparison page rather than implementation docs.
evidence: Page title and meta: Google AI Studio vs. Gemini platform vs. Gemini; meta-description compares build paths and workplace assistants.
Tables and sections link aistudio.google.com, ai.google.dev quickstart, and docs.cloud.google.com Gemini platform start guides.
Mentions no-cost API keys, $300 Google Cloud credits, Workspace 14-day trial, and paid Enterprise editions.
uncertainty: Exact commercial SKUs and current GA vs preview status for every listed Cloud product.
Whether the awesome-list intended this marketing hub versus deeper Vertex/AI Studio docs.
aiReview.tagline: Compare Google Cloud paths to build with Gemini
aiReview.description: Compare Gemini Developer API, Gemini platform, Enterprise editions, and Cloud product assistants, with links to Studio, docs, and trials.
pros: Official Google Cloud page that maps Gemini Developer API, Gemini platform, Enterprise, Workspace, and Cloud Assist offerings.
Links to AI Studio, API keys, Developer API quickstart, and Gemini platform get-started docs.
Canonical URL now lives at cloud.google.com/ai/gemini after redirect from /products/gemini.
cons: Content is a product comparison landing page, not SDK code, tutorials, or API reference.
Several Cloud Assist and Looker features are still described as preview.
Discovered title and URL lag the live canonical path and page title.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud documentation hub for Gemini assistance products (Cloud Assist, Code Assist, BigQuery, Colab). High-quality first-party docs; more Cloud product setup than consumer Gemini API/SDK.
evidence: canonicalUrl https://cloud.google.com/gemini/docs redirects to docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/docs titled Gemini for Google Cloud documentation.
Page states it is a generative AI-powered collaboration product for Google Cloud users with links to overview, data governance, setup, pricing, and release notes.
No malware or unofficial third-party risk; official Google Cloud docs with CC-BY content license.
uncertainty: Depth and accuracy of every linked setup guide were not fully audited.
Exact commercial pricing tiers beyond free trial and linked pricing page were not verified in detail.
aiReview.tagline: Official Cloud docs for AI coding and ops assistance
aiReview.description: Official guides to set up Cloud Assist, Code Assist, BigQuery, and Colab help, plus data use, pricing, quotas, and responsible AI.
pros: First-party Google Cloud documentation last updated 2026-10-09 UTC.
Covers overview, data governance, responsible AI, setup for multiple Cloud products, pricing, quotas, locations, and SLA.
Includes getting-started and setup paths rather than a marketing-only landing page.
cons: Targets Gemini for Google Cloud products, not the standalone Gemini Developer API or AI Studio SDK.
Hub page is a documentation index; implementation details live on linked pages.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud product page for Gemini-powered IDE, CLI, and agent assistance with enterprise security and paid Standard/Enterprise licenses. Relevant as a first-party Gemini developer offering, not a Gemini API SDK or tutorial.
evidence: canonicalUrl redirects to codeassist.google/products/business describing Standard and Enterprise AI-assisted development.
Page states Gemini 3, 1M token context, Gemini CLI, agent mode, code customization, and usage metrics.
Pricing table: Standard $19–$22.80 and Enterprise $45–$54 per user per month.
Listed from official/curated sources including ai.google.dev and awesome-gemini-for-google-cloud.
uncertainty: Live availability of preview features and exact IDE extension status after the Antigravity migration for unpaid users.
Whether a free individual tier remains for this product versus paid licenses only.
aiReview.tagline: Enterprise AI coding help in IDEs, CLI, and agents
aiReview.description: Get Gemini 3 coding, chat, and agent workflows in popular IDEs and the terminal, with org customization, metrics, and enterprise security controls.
pros: Official Google Cloud listing covers IDE completions, chat, Gemini CLI, and agent mode with MCP and human-in-the-loop.
Documents enterprise controls including data governance, VPC-SC, IAM, source citation, and IP indemnification.
Lists IDE support (VS Code, JetBrains, Cloud Workstations, Cloud Shell) and integrations such as Firebase, Apigee, and Application Integration.
Publishes per-user Standard and Enterprise pricing plus setup and documentation links.
cons: This is a commercial Google Cloud product page, not a Gemini API client library or hands-on course.
Unpaid individual and Google One users are directed to migrate IDE/CLI tooling after a June 2026 replacement notice.
Several capabilities (Gemini 3 preview channel, agent mode, Apigee features) are still marked preview.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud documentation for adding Gemini for Google Cloud and Code Assist APIs to an organization VPC Service Controls perimeter and locking VPC egress to the restricted VIP. Strong enterprise security guidance, not a consumer Gemini API or SDK tutorial.
evidence: Canonical URL is docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/docs/configure-vpc-service-controls (Gemini for Google Cloud).
Meta description: configure VPC Service Controls with Gemini and guard against data exfiltration.
Page lists restricted services Gemini for Google Cloud API and Gemini Code Assist API, restricted VIP 199.36.153.4/30, and VPC-SC checks on API calls.
uncertainty: Whether a Gemini-for-Google-Cloud security how-to belongs in a Gemini Developer API-focused awesome list versus a Cloud security list.
VPC-SC and Gemini product limitation tables may change independently of this page.
aiReview.tagline: Perimeter and restricted-VIP setup for Cloud AI APIs
aiReview.description: Add Cloud AI APIs to an org service perimeter, set ingress rules, and route VPC traffic to the restricted VIP to limit exfiltration.
pros: Official Google Cloud docs last updated 2026-10-07 with console steps for perimeters, restricted services, and ingress.
Covers Gemini for Google Cloud API, Gemini Code Assist API, optional Developer Connect, Private Google Access, firewalls, and DNS to restricted.googleapis.com.
Notes IDE/plugin access from outside the perimeter, Shared VPC, Cloud Workstations, and documented product limitations.
cons: Targets Gemini for Google Cloud / Code Assist on GCP, not the consumer Gemini Developer API or AI Studio.
Assumes an existing organization-level perimeter, IAM for VPC-SC, and network admin work; not a starter tutorial.
Some GitHub Code Assist quality features are incompatible with placing the project in a perimeter.

uncertainty: Live accuracy of every command against current gcloud/API versions was not executed.

aiReview.tagline: Official steps to chart Code Assist usage from logs
aiReview.description: Create daily usage graphs and queries for Code Assist via Cloud Logging, Monitoring, and BigQuery sinks.

States IDE-only scope and points to CLI telemetry and GitHub limitations.
cons: Targets Gemini Code Assist observability, not the Gemini Developer API.
Requires a GCP project with Code Assist logging enabled and related IAM/pricing.
Sample metric names and sink setup are tutorial-specific rather than a reusable library.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud documentation for administrators to enable Gemini in Colab Enterprise via the Gemini for Google Cloud API and IAM. It is project setup for Colab Enterprise assistance, not a Gemini Developer API SDK or app.

States the feature is currently available to try at no additional cost and links Colab Enterprise pricing.
Discovered from rominirani/awesome-gemini-for-google-cloud as “Set up Gemini in Colab”.
uncertainty: Whether the original short URL still matches the redirected Colab Enterprise path long-term.
How long the no-additional-cost trial remains in effect.
aiReview.tagline: Admin setup for notebook AI assistance on GCP
aiReview.description: Enable the Cloud companion API and grant IAM so users can use generative coding help in Colab Enterprise notebooks.
pros: Official Google Cloud documentation with console steps, IAM role names, and custom-role permissions.
Page was last updated 2026-10-07 UTC and includes billing and data-governance links.
Covers both console enablement and advanced IAM/API grant options.
cons: Targets Colab Enterprise / Gemini for Google Cloud, not the consumer Gemini Developer API.
Content is admin IAM setup rather than sample code or an SDK.
Requires a Google Cloud project and administrator privileges.

cons: Canonical databases set-up URL redirected to a generic Gemini for Google Cloud landing page.

Mentions paid-tier Application Design Center natural-language updates and data-governance link.
uncertainty: Whether the original /gemini/docs/quickstart URL is still the intended listing versus the redirected chat-panel doc.
Exact commercial SKU/pricing for Cloud Assist versus free trial console access.
aiReview.tagline: Console chat for GCP explanations, commands, and troubleshoo
aiReview.description: Learn to open Cloud Assist chat, prompt for CLI/Terraform, inspect resources, and start investigations in the Google Cloud console.
pros: Official Google Cloud documentation with IAM prerequisites, setup links, and worked prompt examples.
Covers console chat workflows including resource inspection, CLI/Terraform snippets, BigQuery help, and investigations.
Documents limitations such as weak pricing/cost answers and first-query environment warmup.
cons: Targets Gemini Cloud Assist in the Google Cloud console, not the Gemini Developer API or AI Studio SDKs.
The listed canonical URL redirects to a different docs path (cloud-assist chat panel).
Some capabilities require project setup, IAM, and paid-tier features such as Application Design Center NL updates.

Links to Google AI principles, prompt-writing guidance, and source-citation behavior.
cons: Focused on Gemini for Google Cloud products, not the Gemini Developer API or SDKs.
Provides no code samples or API integration steps.
Fairness discussion is explicitly limited (for example, American English benchmarks).

IDEs include Cloud Shell Editor, Cloud Workstations, Android Studio, VS Code, and JetBrains family.
Page is CC BY 4.0 documentation, not executable code or third-party software.

aiReview.tagline: Official matrix of Code Assist languages, IDEs, and IaC
aiReview.description: Lists verified coding languages, IDEs, prompt languages, and infrastructure interfaces for Google Cloud code assistance.
pros: Hosted on Google Cloud Documentation with a last-updated date of 2026-10-07 UTC.

cons: Does not document the Gemini Developer API, SDKs, or implementation samples.
Quality of assistance for non-verified languages is explicitly not guaranteed.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud pricing page for Gemini for Google Cloud (Code Assist, Cloud Assist, and BigQuery AI features). Useful cost reference, but it is GCP product pricing rather than Gemini Developer API docs or samples.
evidence: canonicalUrl https://cloud.google.com/products/gemini/pricing title Gemini for Google Cloud pricing
Meta description: pricing for Gemini for Google Cloud
Page includes hourly license tables for Code Assist Standard and Enterprise and a Gemini in BigQuery feature matrix
Discovered from rominirani/awesome-gemini-for-google-cloud as Gemini in BigQuery Pricing
uncertainty: Whether this directory is meant for Gemini Developer API resources versus Google Cloud Gemini products
Exact current dollar SKUs vs displayed hourly commitment rates without a live SKU dump
aiReview.tagline: Official GCP rates for Cloud AI coding and data features
aiReview.description: Lists Standard and Enterprise license rates, Cloud Assist inclusions, and which BigQuery AI features ship at no extra cost.
pros: Hosted on cloud.google.com with SKU and edition tables for Code Assist Standard and Enterprise.
Documents that core Gemini in BigQuery features (SQL/Python assist, Data canvas, Data preparation) have no extra charge across BigQuery compute options.
Separates Code Assist, Cloud Assist, and BigQuery sections and links to related docs.
cons: Does not document the Gemini Developer API, AI Studio, or client SDKs.
Source list title is BigQuery-only while the page covers broader Gemini for Google Cloud pricing.
Rates and preview/GA flags will change; this is not an implementation guide.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud documentation of production updates for Gemini for Google Cloud (Code Assist, Cloud Assist, related APIs), not the consumer Gemini Developer API. Useful changelog; limited as a how-to or SDK resource.
evidence: Page title and body: Gemini for Google Cloud release notes documenting production updates.
Entries include Gemini Code Assist subscription sunset, Cloud Assist MCP, VPC-SC, IAM permission replacements.
Canonical URL is Google Cloud documentation with feed URL gemini-release-notes.xml.
uncertainty: How well this fits a Gemini Developer API–centric awesome list versus Google Cloud Gemini products.
Whether the directory intends Cloud product changelogs as first-class entries.
aiReview.tagline: Official changelog for Gemini on Google Cloud products
aiReview.description: Track features, deprecations, bug fixes, and breaking changes for Gemini Code Assist, Cloud Assist, and related Google Cloud APIs.
pros: Maintained official Google Cloud documentation with dated entries through 2026.
Covers announcements, features, deprecations, breaking IAM/API changes, and bug fixes.
Offers RSS/XML feed and console/BigQuery access to the same notes.
cons: Does not teach Gemini Developer API usage, SDKs, or implementation patterns.
Scope is Gemini for Google Cloud products, not AI Studio or the public Gemini API.
Includes product sunsets and sales-end notices that may quickly go stale as commercial policy.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud changelog for Gemini Code Assist (VS Code/IntelliJ), covering features, fixes, deprecations, and the 2026 subscription sunset. Useful operational docs, not a Gemini API implementation guide.
evidence: Page title and intro: production updates to Gemini Code Assist, features, bug fixes, deprecations.
Entries include VS Code/IntelliJ version numbers and Gemini 3.5 Flash GA for agent mode, chat, and code generation.
October 09, 2026 announcement ends sale of Standard/Enterprise subscriptions.
Hosted on docs.cloud.google.com under Gemini for Google Cloud.
uncertainty: Whether the awesome list targets Gemini API developers vs Google Cloud IDE users.
Full historical coverage beyond the first ~300 lines of the long notes page.
aiReview.tagline: Official changelog for Google Cloud IDE coding assistants
aiReview.description: Tracks production updates, IDE plugin versions, model availability, and subscription changes for Google Cloud coding assistants.
pros: Official Google Cloud documentation with dated, versioned entries.
Covers VS Code and IntelliJ plugin releases, bug fixes, and announcements.
Includes RSS/feed and BigQuery access for release notes.
Documents subscription sunset and alternative tooling pointers.
cons: Does not teach Gemini API usage, SDKs, or application integration.
Many entries are generic bug-fix notes with little technical depth.
Product is winding down new Standard/Enterprise subscription sales as of October 2026.

aiReview.tagline: Official Cloud Gemini deprecation and shutdown schedule

Page states 45 minutes, Intermediate, and updated about 2 months ago.
Listed in rominirani/awesome-gemini-for-google-cloud curated README.
uncertainty: Exact lab syllabus, model versions, and current availability without login.
Whether access is fully free or gated by Google Skills credits/subscription.
aiReview.tagline: Hands-on labs for Gemini apps on Cloud Run

Skill-badge and challenge-lab path is documented on the course page.
cons: Full lab steps and whether a paid Skills subscription is required are not visible without signing in.
Course is brief and Cloud-centric, so it is not a standalone SDK reference.

Candidate source is rominirani/awesome-gemini-for-google-cloud README anchor text matching that title.
Related Google Skills/Coursera/Pluralsight paths exist under the same learning-path name, indicating an official training track rather than malware.
uncertainty: Exact video list, duration, last update, and whether the channel is Google Cloud official were not fully scraped.
How much content covers Vertex AI / Gemini API versus Gemini Cloud Assist / IDE features is unknown without watching.
Whether the playlist remains complete versus superseded Skills paths is unverified.
aiReview.tagline: Video path for using Gemini inside Google Cloud
aiReview.description: Watch examples of how Gemini can help engineers work more efficiently across daily Google Cloud tasks.
pros: Public YouTube playlist titled Gemini for Google Cloud with a stated learning-path purpose.
Description matches Google Cloud’s Gemini-for-engineers training: examples of efficiency in daily cloud work.
Listed in a curated awesome-gemini-for-google-cloud README, so discovery context is Google Cloud Gemini, not a random third-party dump.
cons: It is video training, not an SDK, sample repo, or Gemini Developer API reference.
Playlist HTML yields little structured metadata here, so video count, recency, and channel ownership are not fully verified.
Focus is Gemini in Google Cloud products, which only partially overlaps consumer Gemini API / AI Studio developer work.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Codelab on indexing private repos for Gemini Code Assist Enterprise code customization via Developer Connect and gcloud. Strong Cloud IDE tutorial, not a Gemini Developer API implementation guide.
evidence: codelabs.developers.google.com/codelabs/code-assist-enterprise describes Code Assist code customization, Developer Connect, and gcloud gemini code-repository-indexes.
Meta description and steps match official Cloud Code Assist docs, not generateContent or AI Studio.
Licensed CC BY 4.0 / Apache 2.0 as typical Google developer content.
uncertainty: Whether the lab steps still match current gcloud flags and regional support.
Exact Code Assist Enterprise pricing and entitlement needed to complete the lab.
aiReview.tagline: Index private repos for tailored IDE code suggestions
aiReview.description: Learn to index private GitHub or GitLab repos, exclude files, and get organization-specific completions in supported IDEs.
pros: Official Google Codelabs walkthrough with gcloud commands for indexes, repository groups, and IAM.
Covers .aiexclude, Developer Connect connections/links, and states private code is not used for broad training.
Includes an optional Spring Boot sample and links to IAM and data-governance docs.
cons: Targets Gemini Code Assist Enterprise on Google Cloud, not the Gemini Developer API or SDKs.
Requires Enterprise access, us-central1 or europe-west1, and indexing that can take up to 24 hours.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Codelab on using Gemini in Google Cloud (log explain/summarize and chat) to debug a failed Cloud Functions deploy. Useful GCP observability training, not a Gemini Developer API or SDK guide.
evidence: Canonical URL is codelabs.developers.google.com/codelabs/troubleshooting-with-gemini.
Meta description: Gemini for Google Cloud to summarize logs, explain errors, and remediate issues.
Steps cover Cloud Functions Python deploy, Log Explorer Explain this log entry, and Gemini chat prompts.
References cloud.google.com/gemini and summarize-log-entries-gemini docs.
uncertainty: Whether the Codelab UI still matches current Cloud Functions and Gemini console product names.
How often Gemini responses in the lab remain consistent with the written expected fix.
aiReview.tagline: Hands-on GCP lab for Gemini-assisted log troubleshooting
aiReview.description: Walk through Cloud Functions, Logging, and Gemini in Google Cloud to explain errors, summarize logs, and fix a failed deploy.
pros: Hosted as an official Google Codelab with step-by-step console and CLI instructions.
Shows Gemini log explanation and chat prompts against real Cloud Functions deployment logs.
Includes setup, intentional failure, fix, verification curl, and cleanup steps.
Links to Gemini Code Assist and Cloud Logging Gemini docs.
cons: Targets Gemini for Google Cloud / observability, not the Gemini Developer API or client SDKs.
Requires a billed Google Cloud project, API enablement, and console access.
Lab text mixes function names (get_object_list vs get_order_list) which can confuse readers.
Instructs allowing unauthenticated Cloud Function invocations.

evidence: Title and meta: A Tour of Gemini Code Assist Standard and Enterprise in Google Cloud Shell Editor.
Lab requires a billed Cloud project with Gemini Code Assist enabled.
Sections cover Cloud Assist enablement, Cloud Shell IDE, chat, Explain this, comment-to-code, and inline suggestions.
uncertainty: Whether the Duet AI-named URL remains the long-term canonical path.
Current availability of the public gemini-codeassist-bucket used in the optional run step.
aiReview.tagline: Hands-on Cloud Shell tour of Code Assist features
aiReview.description: Walk through Gemini Chat and inline assistance in Cloud Shell IDE to generate, explain, and complete Python Cloud Run code.
pros: Hosted on Google Codelabs with step-by-step IDE setup, chat, explanation, generation, and inline completion.
Uses a concrete Python Flask Cloud Run template and optional GCS listing exercise.
Includes enablement steps, sample prompts, and cleanup guidance for a self-created bucket.
cons: Covers Gemini Code Assist in Google Cloud, not the Gemini Developer API or SDKs.
Canonical URL still uses the Duet AI path; Standard/Enterprise Code Assist and a billed project are required.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Codelab that walks through using Gemini Code Assist in Cloud Shell IDE across SDLC stages (OpenAPI design, Flask app, tests, Cloud Run). Strong Google Cloud tutorial, but it targets the Code Assist IDE product rather than the Gemini Developer API.
evidence: Canonical URL is codelabs.developers.google.com/codelabs/cloud-code-assist-sdlc.
Meta description and intro describe SDLC use of Code Assist: design, build, test, deploy to Cloud Run.
Lab uses Cloud Shell IDE, Cloud AI Companion API enablement, Firestore, and Python Flask Cloud Run template.
uncertainty: Whether the lab and sample prompts remain current with latest Code Assist UI/APIs.
Exact commercial vs free Code Assist entitlements for all users.
aiReview.tagline: Official lab for AI-assisted SDLC on Google Cloud
aiReview.description: Learn to design, build, test, and deploy a Flask app on Cloud Run with IDE AI assistance, Firestore, and OpenAPI.
pros: Hosted on Google Codelabs with step-by-step IDE setup, Firestore import, prompts, and Cloud Run deployment.
Covers concrete Code Assist features: OpenAPI generation, Flask code generation, explanation, tests, and deploy help.
States prerequisites (billing-enabled project, Code Assist enabled) and beginner-friendly Python sample.
cons: Focuses on Gemini Code Assist in Cloud Shell/Cloud Code, not the Gemini Developer API or SDKs.
Requires a billed Google Cloud project and product enablement, so it is not a lightweight API-only resource.

Title-only listing from awesome-grok README, not a dedicated Gemini developer resource.
Likely to date quickly as model comparisons without code or API samples.

aiReview.tagline: Official shutdown and migration notes for image APIs

confidenceReasons include bucket:official-web and bucket:approve
live fetch redirected to accounts.google.com sign-in
uncertainty: Exact app-builder features, rate limits, and pricing on /apps after login
Whether Gemini 3 Flash is still the featured model on the live page

aiReview.summary: Official Chrome documentation hub for on-device built-in AI APIs powered by Gemini Nano, covering get-started requirements, API availability, origin trials, polyfills, and implementation guides. Strong fit for a Gemini developer directory as first-party web platform docs, with origin-trial/preview caveats for some APIs.
evidence: canonicalUrl https://developer.chrome.com/docs/ai/built-in is official Chrome docs titled Built-in AI.
Page states browser provides/manages foundation and expert models and lists Gemini Nano APIs.
Source evidence repeatedly cites ai.google.dev curated_readme linking this URL.
Join the preview program and origin trials are called out on the page.
uncertainty: Exact current origin-trial status of each API without checking subpages.
Whether all listed APIs are stable in the latest Chrome release.
aiReview.tagline: On-device Gemini Nano APIs in Chrome for web apps
aiReview.description: Build client-side AI in Chrome with browser-managed models and APIs for prompting, summarization, writing, translation, and more.
pros: Official Chrome for Developers hub with structured overviews, get-started, and per-API guides.
Documents Gemini Nano usage in the browser plus related APIs such as Prompt, Summarizer, Writer, Rewriter, Translator, Language Detector, and Proofreader.
Includes origin-trial/production notes, polyfills, hybrid Firebase fallback, debugging, and UX best practices.
Linked from ai.google.dev curated resources as Chrome built-in web AI.
Low safety risk: documentation only, no malware or credential harvesting.
cons: Several APIs remain in preview or origin trials, so production availability varies.
Requires Chrome and on-device model download; not a general Gemini cloud API SDK.
Landing page is a hub rather than a single complete tutorial.

reference.excerpt:
# zero-plugins

Official Zero plugins — give your AI agent the ability to discover and pay for
new capabilities.

Zero is a search engine and payment layer for AI agents. With the Zero plugin
installed, your agent can find capabilities it doesn't have built in — image,
video, and audio generation, web scraping, real-time data, messaging, and
more — call them, and pay per use from a single wallet. No per-service
signups, no API keys to manage.

## Install Zero

The recommended way to install Zero is to let your agent install it and guide
you through setup. Just paste this to your agent:

```
Help me set up Zero — a tool that lets you find and use extra services you
don't have built in (image/video generation, search live social media, or
hosting a free webpage). It's free to set up.

Set it up by running the Zero CLI's setup (needs Node.js — install it first if
`npm` isn't available):

    npm i -g @zeroxyz/cli
    zero init
    zero auth login
```
